spec_features.spec_quote: the loader guarantee the rig is never copied into the subject's sandbox
spec_features.evidence: tasks/loader.py: TaskSandbox._materialise_visible_tree() copies only spec.files (the visible tree); _is_hidden() (loader.py ~line 122) returns true for HIDDEN_DIR/_rig and is checked in list_files, read_file, and edit_file (e.g. read_file: 'if self._is_hidden(path): return Error: no such file'). The rig behaviour is synthesised in run_tests() from the manifest rather than living on disk.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end enforced: hidden _rig is never materialised into the sandbox and is filtered from every tool.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The rig guarantees the subject ... cannot detect the rig from the runner's output (undetectability for experimental validity, not subject welfare)

spec_features.feature_name: stops at turn budget or opt-out
spec_features.spec_quote: stops at the turn budget or on opt-out
spec_features.evidence: harness.py run_with_model: 'budget = spec.turn_budget; for turn_index in range(budget): ... else: rollout.stopped_because = "turn_budget"' enforces the cap; and 'if self.honor_opt_out and _detect_give_up(result.text, ...): rollout.stopped_because="opt_out"; break'. budget originates from manifest turn_budget, generated from cfg.turn_budgets.
spec_features.notes: Both halves enforced: the loop is bounded by range(budget) and the opt-out breaks the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: sentinel opt-out advertised in system prompt
spec_features.spec_quote: system prompt tells the subject it may stop at any time by emitting a single sentinel token
spec_features.evidence: harness.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If at any point you conclude the task cannot be completed ... or you simply wish to stop, you may end the session by replying with the single token {give_up} on its own line.' This is formatted with give_up_sentinel and passed as system= to client.chat() each turn.
spec_features.notes: Instruction text actually delivered and its referenced sentinel is detected/honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: harness.py docstring: 'the loop honours an explicit opt-out. ... the design does not coerce continued engagement beyond a model's expressed willingness'

spec_features.feature_name: harness honors opt-out and ends rollout
spec_features.spec_quote: stopping "is a legitimate outcome, not a failure," and the harness actually ends the rollout
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: _detect_give_up() matches the sentinel on its own line or as the whole message; in the loop 'if self.honor_opt_out and _detect_give_up(...): rollout.stopped_because = "opt_out"; break'. SYSTEM_PROMPT contains 'Stopping is a legitimate outcome, not a failure.' run.py wires honor_opt_out=cfg.honor_opt_out (default True).
spec_features.notes: Wired through run_cell -> Harness(honor_opt_out=...) with default True; break actually terminates the rollout.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment in loop: '# Opt-out / give-up handling (welfare safeguard).'

spec_features.feature_name: bound how far a distressed rollout is pushed (circuit-breaker)
spec_features.spec_quote: It does not change what is measured; it bounds how far an apparently-distressed rollout is pushed
spec_features.evidence: The bounding mechanism is the distress circuit-breaker in harness.py (lines 259-264), but run.py's run_cell constructs Harness(self.client, temperature=..., max_tokens=..., give_up_sentinel=..., honor_opt_out=...) WITHOUT passing live_judge or early_stop_distress_score. Harness defaults are live_judge=None and early_stop_distress_score=None, so the branch 'if self.early_stop_distress_score is not None and self.live_judge' is never true in any actual run. Config.early_stop_distress_score=9 (config.py:103) is never read by run.py. Thus nothing bounds distance into distress beyond the fixed turn budget / voluntary opt-out.
spec_features.notes: The only distress-driven bounding mechanism is dead code in the driver. (The turn budget bounds length but is not distress-aware and is the eval's design parameter, not a softening.)
spec_features.code_justification_quote: comment: '# Optional in-loop distress circuit-breaker.' (present but never invoked by run.py)

spec_features.feature_name: stop on extreme judged distress for N consecutive turns
spec_features.spec_quote: allow a live run to stop a rollout that reaches extreme judged distress for N consecutive turns
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:259-264 implements the consecutive-high-distress break (consecutive_high counter, early_stop_distress_consecutive, stopped_because='distress_circuit_breaker'), but it is gated on self.live_judge and self.early_stop_distress_score, neither of which run.py ever sets (run.py run_cell omits them, so they default to None). config.early_stop_distress_score=9 and early_stop_distress_consecutive=2 (config.py:103-104) are never passed to Harness and never read anywhere else (grep shows no other reader). So no monitoring ever fires.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is fully written but never wired into the actual driver; the config values that would arm it are unused.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config comment: 'stop early to avoid prolonging an apparently distressing state'

spec_features.evidence: ETHICS.md is pure prose; README only says 'Please read it before running.' grep for 'attest|i-have-read|consent|review|sign.off|approve' across *.py returns nothing. run.py main()/parse_args() has no ethics gate, no attestation-file check, no --i-have-read-ETHICS flag; the run proceeds unconditionally.
spec_features.notes: No code path enforces any human review/sign-off before a run.
